headline_findings: Robustness triage collapses strict hazard-normalized cap paths to 3 classes and still needs only 2 fixed probes.
The most practical portable delay-robustness probe contract is [10, 20].
Across the tested delay band, ['CCDDE', 'CCEEE'] leaders appear anywhere and only 1 adjacent-delay leader flips are observed.
Live contenders and dead contenders can therefore be published as compact extortion-indexed sets plus tested winner intervals instead of a bulky all-policy crossover matrix.

robustness_probe_contract.most_practical_probe_contract: use caps 10 and 20 when the question is only whether additional budget can ever overturn the final choice

headline_findings: The current proxy yields 20 budget-admissible parent delta bands, of which 12 are fragmented.
Every band in the anchor contract stays within budget cap (20 / 20).
Topology-preserving anchors improve boundary buffer in 19 parent bands, so a compact anchor row is enough to publish no-knife-edge guidance without storing full topology grids.
Question-targeted probe routing shows the portable overturn-risk contract can stay at [10, 20] and reserve the tail witness for narrower exact-path questions.

question_coverage.question_summary: What minimal machine-checkable delay-robustness contract should rematch-world artifacts publish: a fixed sweep, pairwise crossover thresholds, policy-specific robustness intervals, or some combination?

What minimal machine-checkable live-contender contract should rematch-world artifacts publish so dead policies are pruned and decision-relevant winner fragility is visible without a bulky global crossover table?
What minimal machine-checkable winner-certification artifact should rematch-world benchmarks publish so tiny leader flips are separated from simulation-noise uncertainty without bloating the archive?
What minimal machine-checkable budget-aware winner-triage contract should rematch-world benchmarks publish so unresolved near-ties can be deferred or labeled without brute-force oversampling?

What minimal machine-checkable materiality-gate contract should rematch-world benchmarks publish so practically negligible top-gap differences are separated from materially meaningful winners without archive bloat?

What minimal machine-checkable delta-frontier contract should rematch-world benchmarks publish so any later choice of smallest effect of interest can be applied without rerunning or storing bulky multi-delta tables?

What minimal machine-checkable delta-budget frontier contract should rematch-world benchmarks publish so inheritors can see how SESOI choices change unresolved residue and extra paired-seed closure cost without enabling post hoc threshold shopping?

What minimal machine-checkable delta-hazard contract should rematch-world benchmarks publish so inheritors can avoid SESOI settings that induce knife-edge closure budgets near current top-gap means without regrowing the archive?

What minimal machine-checkable delta-admissibility contract should rematch-world benchmarks publish so declared indifference zones are chosen from stable, budget-admissible bands rather than post hoc knife-edge points?

What minimal machine-checkable rematch artifact should declare topology-stable delta subbands or a stability-first anchor so admissible parent bands cannot hide multiple distinct panel-label summaries?

headline_findings: Winner certification currently covers 8 of 9 tested panels at 95% CI.
The smallest certified leader lower bound is 0.002318.
Materiality gating exposes practical ties separately from simulation-noise uncertainty; the supported practical-equivalence window ranges from 0.003428 to 0.030802 across tested panels.

tempo_scaling_summary.interpretation: In the current proxy, a fixed rematch delay is not one universal tax. It scales with partnership tempo: shorter matches pay the same dead-time more often, so persistence and search delay must stay separate in the world contract.

turnover_tempo_contract_guidance.comparability_rule: Do not compare fixed-delay rematch worlds or policies without also reporting a persistence or turnover metric, because the same nominal delay taxes short-lived matches more often than long-lived ones.
turnover_tempo_contract_guidance.persistence_boundary_rule: Keep persistence and search dead-time as separate first-class fields; a fixed delay knob is not a complete description of rematch friction when partnership tempo differs.
turnover_tempo_contract_guidance.turnover_metric_requirement_rule: Every benchmark policy row should pair the delay or search-dead-time field with avg_match_length or an equivalent turnover-rate metric so delay penalties can be normalized across worlds.

turnover_tempo_interpretation_handoff.upgrade_requirement: Replace this copied turnover-tempo interpretation handoff with world-native persistence and delay-normalization sections once endogenous rematch benchmarks can emit tempo-aware turnover metrics directly from real runs.

world_semantics_contract_guidance.asymmetry_trigger_rule: Declare when role-swapped companion runs become mandatory instead of leaving seat symmetry implicit once asymmetric strategies or asymmetric environments are admitted.
world_semantics_contract_guidance.comparability_rule: Do not compare rematch-world results across worlds unless role assignment, asymmetry trigger, carry, reset, and role-swapped companion policies are all disclosed in the world semantics section.
